_why: Porch & Party's first two weeks from the content engine (porch-and-party brain, FILLER CONTENT TO 31 DEC and CONTENT ENGINE, 19 Nov 2026): one reel a day to TikTok, Instagram and the Facebook Page from Sat 21 Nov, photo sets about three a week, Memphis evening. real: = the owner's own job photos, shown as our work; ai: = the site's AI scenes and gen: = new scenes made free on Workers AI (engine/imagine.mjs), both never captioned as a job we did and never labelled in the caption (TikTok's own AI switch is set). Mix: real work 6, holiday ideas 6, engagement 3, tips 3, how it works 1, office parties 1. No prices, no voice, music + on-screen words, the request link in every caption.

generate.grazing-board-december.jpg: A real photograph of a simple grazing board for a December party on a wooden dining table in a Memphis home, in warm evening lamp light. One long walnut board holds three cheeses cut in wedges (a white brie, an orange cheddar, a blue cheese), a short S-shaped line of overlapping salami slices, two small bunches of red grapes, a small white bowl of pecans, a short row of crackers, and three small sprigs of rosemary tucked at the board's edge. Beside the board, one small white bowl of apricot jam with a wooden spoon. Plenty of bare wood shows between the foods. Behind, out of focus, a dining room with a small lit Christmas tree. Camera at standing eye level from a three-quarter angle, the board running diagonally across the frame between about 30% and 60% down; the upper third is the soft background and the lower third is plain wooden tabletop. 35mm lens, natural colours, slight film grain, slightly imperfect white balance.
generate.office-grazing-ready.jpg: A real photograph of a long folding table in an ordinary Memphis office break room, set for a December holiday party just before anyone arrives, early evening. A plain white tablecloth; on it, laid straight down the length of the table on a runner of brown kraft paper, a grazing spread in loose groups: wedges of three cheeses, folded salami, red grapes, crackers and small sprigs of rosemary, with paper showing between the groups; a short stack of small white plates at the near end. Behind the table, a plain white wall, a window with the dusky city outside, and a small lit Christmas tree in the corner. Warm light from a floor lamp and the tree. Camera at standing eye level from one end of the table, the table running diagonally from the lower right toward the window, the food between about 30% and 60% down; the top third is wall and window; the bottom quarter is the plain white tablecloth edge and grey floor. 35mm lens, natural colours, slight film grain, slightly imperfect white balance.
generate.office-lobby-garland.jpg: A real photograph of the small front lobby of an ordinary Memphis office on a December evening, set for the holiday party just before anyone arrives. A plain wooden reception desk with a fresh green garland, small warm-white lights tucked unevenly into it, draped along its front edge; a small lit Christmas tree beside the desk; one upholstered armchair against the wall; a tall plain window on the side wall with the dark street outside; a grey tiled floor. The desktop is bare except for a brass table lamp, which gives warm light with the tree. Camera at standing eye level from the middle of the lobby, the desk across the middle of the frame; the top third is plain painted wall and ceiling; the lower third is plain floor. 35mm lens, natural colours, slight film grain, slightly imperfect white balance.
generate.tg-table-at-home.jpg: Photo-real vertical photograph, shot on a full-frame camera, warm evening light: a long Thanksgiving dining table in a Memphis home styled for twelve, a wide wooden grazing board of cheeses, grapes, figs, nuts and crackers down the middle, low magnolia leaves and small white pumpkins, cream linen napkins, amber glass candle holders lit, empty chairs, nobody at the table.

xmas-porch-haint-door.jpg.prompt: Edit this photograph. Keep the house, ceiling, door, wreath, doormat, the shape of the steps and the camera exactly the same; the door, its handle and the wreath do not change. Add a fresh cedar garland up and over the door frame, each side hanging straight down beside the frame and ending just below the height of the door handle, with small warm-white lights tucked unevenly into it, some deep in the branches, some closer together; a strand of warm-white lights along the front edge of each step; two brass lanterns with lit white pillar candles on the top step, a tall one on the left and a shorter one on the right; a terracotta pot with a small spruce tree on each side of the door, the right one a little shorter and fuller. The new lights cast a little warm glow on the siding and steps. Add a slight natural film grain.

generate.xmas-porch-haint-one-wreath.jpg: A real photograph of the front door of a Memphis house on a December evening in the blue hour just after sunset, from the front walk at standing eye level. A deep covered front porch with painted white wood siding and a pale blue-green painted porch ceiling, the soft haint blue of old Southern porches, softly lit by the last blue evening light and a warm glow from the door's small window. A natural stained-wood front door with a small glass window and a simple brass handle on its right side. One full evergreen wreath with a deep red velvet bow on the door; the door frame, the siding and the three white-painted wooden steps are otherwise bare. A plain brown coir doormat. The painted grey porch floor either side of the door is empty boards, and the porch posts are plain white. A few dry brown oak leaves on the bottom step. The pale blue-green ceiling and plain siding above the door fill the top third of the frame as plain painted boards; the door spans about 33-75% down; the three steps fill the bottom quarter. 35mm lens, natural colours, slight film grain, slightly imperfect white balance.
generate.xmas-white-column-porch.jpg: Photo-real vertical photograph, shot on a full-frame camera in early evening: a Southern porch with white columns in Memphis dressed for Christmas, fresh garland with warm white lights wrapped up the columns, wreaths with red ribbons on the tall windows, two white rocking chairs with red plaid blankets, lanterns glowing on the porch floor, magnolia leaves in the garland.
generate.yard-connect-four-nov.jpg: A real photograph of a giant four-in-a-row yard game standing on dormant straw-tan Bermuda grass in a Memphis backyard in late November at dusk. The game is about four feet tall: a blue-painted wooden game on two splayed A-frame legs. The upright playing board is one continuous flat panel painted the same blue as the legs, with a small drop opening above each column along its top edge, and 7 columns and 6 rows of identical round holes in perfectly even rows and columns. Only the bottom row holds discs: three flat round discs, red, yellow, red, side by side in the three middle columns, resting at the very bottom. All the remaining holes above them are empty, and the yard shows through them. On the grass beside the right leg, two short stacks of flat round discs, one red, one yellow. Behind: a weathered wooden privacy fence with one strand of warm-white string lights, a bare oak tree, scattered brown oak leaves. Soft last daylight lights the front of the game evenly. Camera at chest height, slight three-quarter angle, the whole game in frame and centred left to right: its top edge about 33% down the frame and its feet about 62% down, the board filling a little over half the frame width, open straw-tan grass filling everything below. 35mm lens, natural colours, slight film grain, slightly imperfect white balance.

office-games-breakroom-v2.jpg.prompt: Edit this photograph. Keep the blue four-in-a-row game exactly as it is, at the same size and in the same position: the same board, the same open holes, the same legs, and the red and yellow disc stacks beside its right leg. Replace everything around it with an ordinary Memphis office break room in the early evening, set for a December holiday party before anyone arrives. The grass becomes plain clean grey office carpet, filling the floor to the bottom of the frame. A few steps behind the game, one plain white back wall with no windows fills the background from the top of the frame down to the carpet; through every open hole in the board, the white wall shows. To the right of the game, against that wall, the near end of a long table with a plain white tablecloth, a brown kraft-paper runner and a short stack of small white plates. To the left of the game, against the same wall and partly showing beside the board, a small lit Christmas tree about four feet tall on a plain white tree skirt, and at the left edge of the frame a floor lamp with a plain white shade. Soft warm indoor light from the lamp and the tree falls on the game. Keep the camera the same. Add a slight natural film grain.

generate.yard-cornhole-one.jpg: A real photograph of one cornhole board set up on dormant straw-tan Bermuda grass in a Memphis backyard in late November at dusk. The board is lightly used natural pine with visible wood grain and a few scuffs and dirt marks on its edges, two feet wide and four feet long, with a four-inch wooden side frame. Its low front edge rests on the grass nearest the camera, and it slopes up away from the camera to its back end, which stands about one foot off the grass on two folding wooden legs. One round six-inch hole, centred side to side, about nine inches from the raised back end. Soft last daylight falls evenly on the board. Camera crouched about three feet above the grass, about seven feet in front of the board's low front edge, looking straight along it and tilted slightly down: the board sits centred, its low front edge about 58% down and its raised back end about 36% down, filling about two fifths of the frame width, the hole a wide dark oval near its far end. Behind it, open straw-tan lawn with scattered brown oak leaves runs back to a weathered wooden privacy fence across the frame about 10-25% down, with one strand of warm-white string lights along its top about 12% down, bare tree branches and a thin strip of deep blue dusk sky above it at the very top. Open straw-tan grass with scattered brown leaves fills the frame from 62% down to the bottom edge. 35mm lens, natural colours, slight film grain, slightly imperfect white balance.
